approach_quality.justification: The strategy was very direct. It identified a clear algorithmic bottleneck in the evictor and fixed it. While the block manager changes are micro-optimizations, they are standard practice in high-performance Python code.

execution_quality.justification: The edits were syntactically perfect and logically sound. The agent followed the requirement to create a reproduction script and verify, though the logs show a very rapid transition to the final solution.

key_decisions: Refactoring LRUEvictor.evict from a 4-pass search to a single-pass search.
Localizing method lookups (gpu_allocator.free) in BlockSpaceManager._free_block_table to reduce attribute access overhead in loops.
Adding a conditional check in _maybe_promote_last_block to avoid redundant assignments to the block table.
Using a local reference for set.update in get_block_table to speed up sequence group processing.
optimization_techniques: Attribute lookup caching (Local variables for methods)
missed_opportunities: Could have explored using a Priority Queue (heapq) for the evictor if the free table was large, though O(n) is often faster for Python dictionaries of moderate size.
Could have checked for __slots__ usage in physical block classes to reduce memory pressure.
